---
title: "Story: The Impact of Daily Activity"
subtitle: "How exercise and movement shape a Golden Retriever's lifespan"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: story-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

library(tidyverse)

dogs <- read_csv("golden_retrievers.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(activity_level = factor(activity_level, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")))

dogs |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = activity_level, y = lifespan_years, fill = activity_level)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "The Power of Play: Daily Exercise and Longevity",
    subtitle = "Dogs with high daily activity live nearly a full year longer than sedentary dogs",
    x = "Activity Level",
    y = "Life Expectancy (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
```

When looking at factors influencing a Golden Retriever's health, diet and weight often get the most attention. However, our dataset of 10,000 dogs reveals another critical factor: daily physical activity.

Golden Retrievers with high activity levels live to an average of **12.2 years**, compared to **11.3 years** for dogs with low activity levels. Regular walks, fetching, and active playtime provide cardiovascular benefits and joint mobility that appear to add nearly an entire extra year of companionship.

### Fascinating Facts About Golden Retrievers

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
#### 1. Scottish Highland Origins
The breed originated in 1868 in the rugged Scottish Highlands. Dudley Marjoribanks (Lord Tweedmouth) crossed a Yellow Retriever named "Nous" with a Tweed Water Spaniel named "Belle" to produce swimming, resilient gundogs suited for retrieving waterfowl across land and cold rivers.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
#### 2. The Legendary "Soft Mouth"
Golden Retrievers were bred with such gentle jaw control that they can comfortably carry a raw egg in their mouth without breaking it. This trait was essential so they could retrieve game birds without damaging them.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
#### 3. Emotional Radar and Empathy
Goldens possess an extraordinarily high sensitivity to human vocal tones and emotional cues. Combined with their eager-to-please temperament, this makes them the world's #1 breed for guide work, medical alert, and emotional therapy.
:::

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple"}
#### 4. The Exercise Longevity Dividend
As our data demonstrates, regular play isn't just entertainment—it's preventive medicine. Maintaining a high daily activity routine is associated with up to **0.9 additional years of life expectancy**, helping dogs preserve lean muscle and healthy joints into their senior years.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
#### 5. The Morris Lifetime Study & Lifespan Research
The [Morris Animal Foundation Golden Retriever Lifetime Study](https://www.morrisanimalfoundation.org/article/golden-retriever-lifetime-study-2026-update) has tracked over 3,000 Golden Retrievers to investigate why the breed's average life expectancy has fallen from 16–17 years decades ago to 10–12 years today. With cancer accounting for roughly 75% of deaths in the cohort, the landmark study focuses on risk factors across genetics, lifestyle, and early detection.
:::
